prompt: Name as many characters from Christmas movies, TV specials, songs and stories as you can
answers: Santa Claus / Father Christmas / St Nick / Kris Kringle
Santa's reindeer (all eight together count as one answer)
The Christmas ghosts (Past, Present and Yet to Come count as one answer)
note: Santa counts once under any name (Father Christmas, St Nick, Kris Kringle). Santa's eight reindeer count as one answer between them; Rudolph counts on his own. The three ghosts from A Christmas Carol are one answer. Die Hard counts as a Christmas movie. Accept any other named character best known from a Christmas film, TV special, song, story or ballet, and Christmas folklore figures too. Don't count Nativity figures (they have their own list), famous characters who just appear in a Christmas special (Mickey Mouse, Kermit, Mr. Bean, Charlie Brown), or unnamed ones ('an elf', 'a snowman').

prompt: Name as many Disney or Pixar animated movies as you can
answers: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
Winnie the Pooh / The Many Adventures of Winnie the Pooh
note: A numbered sequel counts together with its original as one answer (Toy Story 1-5, Frozen 2, Cars 2 and 3, Incredibles 2, Inside Out 2, Moana 2, Zootopia 2). Sequels with a different name count separately (Finding Dory, Monsters University, Ralph Breaks the Internet, The Rescuers Down Under). Smaller Disney animated films count too (A Goofy Movie, The Tigger Movie, Planes, Tinker Bell, DuckTales the Movie), and so does The Nightmare Before Christmas. Accept any other Disney or Pixar animated feature. A remake doesn't add an answer, and mostly live-action films don't count (Mary Poppins, Enchanted, Who Framed Roger Rabbit, Pete's Dragon, Maleficent). Films Disney bought later don't count (Anastasia and Ice Age were made by Fox), and neither do other studios' hits (Shrek, Kung Fu Panda, How to Train Your Dragon, Despicable Me, Minions, Spider-Verse).

prompt: Name as many things you might put on a Christmas tree as you can
note: 'Ornaments' and 'baubles' are the same answer. Any named ornament shape counts separately (bells, snowflakes, Santas, snowmen, reindeer, birds, nutcrackers, hearts). Popcorn and cranberry strings count separately from garland. 'Tree topper' counts only if neither star nor angel has been ticked. Presents and the tree skirt don't count (they go under the tree), and neither do stockings (they hang on the mantel).

prompt: Name as many Beatles songs as you can
answers: I Want to Hold Your Hand
Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds
Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
With a Little Help from My Friends
Got to Get You into My Life
note: Accept any other genuine Beatles song, including covers they released (Twist and Shout) and the later singles Free as a Bird, Real Love and Now and Then. Solo and Wings hits don't count: Imagine, Give Peace a Chance, Instant Karma!, Happy Xmas (War Is Over), Stand by Me, My Sweet Lord, Live and Let Die, Band on the Run, Maybe I'm Amazed, Mull of Kintyre, Wonderful Christmastime.

prompt: Name as many movies or TV specials with 'Christmas' in the title as you can
answers: It's a Very Merry Muppet Christmas Movie
note: TV movies and TV specials count; individual episodes of a series don't. Each title counts once: remakes with the same title count once, and so do numbered sequels (The Christmas Chronicles 2 = The Christmas Chronicles). A sequel with a different title counts separately (A Christmas Story Christmas). Accept any other real film or special with Christmas in its title, Hallmark and Netflix films included. Don't count Christmas films without the word in the title: Elf, Home Alone, Love Actually, The Polar Express, The Santa Clause, Miracle on 34th Street, It's a Wonderful Life, Die Hard, Klaus, or The Grinch (2018).

prompt: Name as many pizza toppings as you can
note: Different meats, cheeses and peppers each count separately (salami and pepperoni; mozzarella and feta; jalapeños and green peppers). Plain 'cheese' counts once. Accept any other real pizza topping.

prompt: Name as many famous elves as you can
answers: Hermey (the elf who wants to be a dentist)
Jingle (The Year Without a Santa Claus)
Jangle (The Year Without a Santa Claus)
Wise Old Elf (Ben & Holly's Little Kingdom)
note: Buddy counts (he was raised as an elf). Snap, Crackle and Pop are three answers, and Jingle and Jangle are two. Elves from The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit count, Elrond included, and so do Harry Potter's house-elves. The Elf on the Shelf counts once. Hobbits, dwarves, fairies (Tinker Bell), gnomes, pixies, leprechauns and Smurfs don't count, and neither do actors (Will Ferrell) or Link from Zelda (he's a Hylian). Unnamed elves don't count ('Santa's elves', the shoemaker's elves). Accept any other named elf from a book, film, TV show, game or advert.

prompt: Name as many board games as you can
answers: Snakes and Ladders / Chutes and Ladders
note: Count any game played on a board, including kids' classics (Guess Who?, Battleship, Connect 4, Mouse Trap, Operation, Hungry Hungry Hippos). Different editions of one game count once (Monopoly Junior = Monopoly). Ludo and Parcheesi count separately; Pachisi = Parcheesi. Tile, card, dice and word games without a board don't count (dominoes, Rummikub, Bananagrams, Boggle, Scattergories, Codenames, Uno, Exploding Kittens, Yahtzee), and neither do Jenga or Twister. Accept any other real board game.

prompt: Name as many songs with 'Christmas' in the title as you can
answers: All I Want for Christmas Is You
Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas
It's Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas
We Wish You a Merry Christmas
I Wish It Could Be Christmas Everyday
You Make It Feel Like Christmas
note: 'Xmas' and 'Christmastime' count as Christmas. Only the English word counts, so Feliz Navidad and Mele Kalikimaka don't. Songs without the word don't count either: Jingle Bell Rock, Let It Snow!, Santa Baby, Mistletoe and Wine, Fairytale of New York. Accept any other real song with Christmas in its title.

prompt: Name as many Harry Potter characters as you can
answers: Barty Crouch (Sr. and Jr. count as two)
note: Harry himself doesn't count, because he's named in the question. Accept any other named character from the books or films, including Fantastic Beasts, animals, ghosts and portraits. A surname alone counts if it means one person (Snape, Hagrid, McGonagall); 'Dumbledore' alone = Albus. A family name shared by several characters needs a first name too (Weasley, Potter, Malfoy, Dursley). One person with two names counts once (Voldemort = Tom Riddle, Wormtail = Peter Pettigrew).

prompt: Name as many traditional Christmas carols as you can
answers: It Came Upon the Midnight Clear
Angels We Have Heard on High
Go Tell It on the Mountain
Angels from the Realms of Glory
Lo, How a Rose E'er Blooming
We Wish You a Merry Christmas
note: Church carols, hymns and old folk carols count, and so do old songs that carolers sing (Jingle Bells, We Wish You a Merry Christmas, O Christmas Tree, The Twelve Days of Christmas, Up on the Housetop, Jolly Old Saint Nicholas). Carol of the Bells and The Little Drummer Boy count too. Songs that became famous as pop records or in films don't: White Christmas, Frosty the Snowman, Rudolph, Let It Snow!, Jingle Bell Rock, Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town, Silver Bells, Do You Hear What I Hear?, Mary's Boy Child, Little Donkey, Mary, Did You Know?. A foreign-language title counts as the same carol as its English version (Stille Nacht = Silent Night; Adeste Fideles = O Come, All Ye Faithful). Accept any other genuine traditional carol or Christmas hymn.

prompt: Name as many Marvel superheroes as you can
note: A real name counts as the hero (Tony Stark = Iron Man), and each hero name counts once (Peter Parker and Miles Morales are both Spider-Man). Spider-Gwen (Gwen Stacy, called Spider-Woman in the Spider-Verse films) and Spider-Woman (Jessica Drew) are two answers. Anti-heroes count (Deadpool, Venom, the Punisher), and so do heroes without powers (Nick Fury, Shuri, Coulson). Accept any other Marvel hero or heroine from the comics, films or TV. Teams don't count (Avengers, X-Men, Guardians of the Galaxy, Fantastic Four), and neither do villains (Thanos, Red Skull, Ultron) or DC heroes (Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman, The Flash, Aquaman).

prompt: Name as many Christmas desserts and sweet treats from around the world as you can
answers: Christmas pudding / plum pudding / figgy pudding
note: It has to be a sweet treat that's special to Christmas somewhere in the world. Desserts families just happen to serve then don't count (pumpkin or pecan pie, apple pie, brownies, ice cream). Drinks (eggnog, mulled wine) and savory dishes don't count either. Regional spiced biscuits each count separately from gingerbread (Lebkuchen, pepparkakor, speculaas, pfeffernüsse). Teams don't need to name the country. Names separated by a slash are one answer.

prompt: Name as many ice cream flavors as you can
note: Any real flavor counts, including sorbet, gelato and brand flavors (Cherry Garcia, Phish Food, Moose Tracks). Small variations count once (vanilla = French vanilla; chocolate = dark chocolate), but chocolate chip and mint chocolate chip are their own flavors.

prompt: Name as many main courses and side dishes from a Christmas dinner as you can
note: Desserts and drinks don't count. Different meats and fish count separately, and so do different potato dishes (roast, mashed, scalloped). Dishes from other countries' Christmas dinners count (tamales, carp, pierogi, tourtière). 'Vegetables' or 'seafood' on its own doesn't count, so the team has to name them.

prompt: Name as many Star Wars characters as you can
note: One person with two names counts once (Anakin = Darth Vader, Palpatine = Darth Sidious, Ben Solo = Kylo Ren, Grogu = Baby Yoda). Species, troops and job titles don't count (Ewok, Wookiee, Jawa, stormtrooper, Jedi). Accept any other named character from the films or TV series.

prompt: Name as many characters from the Nativity story as you can
note: People, angels and animals all count. 'Wise men', 'Magi' and 'kings' are one answer, but their traditional names Caspar, Melchior and Balthazar each count separately. School-play roles count even though the Bible doesn't mention them (innkeeper, donkey, ox, camels). Gabriel counts separately from 'angels'. The Little Drummer Boy doesn't count (he comes from a 1941 song). Objects don't count either: the star, the manger or the Wise Men's gifts.

prompt: Name as many sports played with a ball as you can
note: Badminton (shuttlecock), ice hockey (puck), curling (stone) and ultimate frisbee (disc) don't count. 'Hockey' on its own counts as field hockey. 'Football' on its own counts as whichever kind the team means, and naming the other kind later counts too. Versions of one sport count once (beach volleyball = volleyball, futsal = soccer, rugby league = rugby union = rugby, T-ball = Wiffle ball = baseball). Softball, kickball and rounders count separately from baseball, and pool and snooker count separately too. Accept any other real sport played with a ball.

prompt: Name as many ways to say 'Christmas' or 'Merry Christmas' in other languages as you can
answers: Vrolijk Kerstfeest / Prettig Kerstfeest / Zalig Kerstfeest / Fijne Kerst / Kerstmis (Dutch)
God jul / Jul (Swedish; also used in Norwegian and Danish)
Sretan Božić / Srećan Božić / Božić (Croatian, Serbian, Bosnian)
Selamat Natal / Selamat Hari Natal (Indonesian, Malay)
Krismasi Njema / Heri ya Krismasi / Krismasi (Swahili)
Chúc mừng Giáng Sinh / Giáng Sinh vui vẻ / Giáng Sinh (Vietnamese)
note: One answer per language: the word for Christmas (Navidad, Noël, Weihnachten) and the full greeting (Feliz Navidad) both score, but only once per language. The team must say the word or phrase; naming a language alone doesn't count. Rough pronunciation is fine. The same word or phrase scores only once even if several languages use it (God jul; Natal; Noël). English words don't count (Xmas, Yule, Happy Christmas). Accept any other real language's word or greeting.

prompt: Name as many James Bond movies as you can
answers: The Man with the Golden Gun
note: Casino Royale counts once, whether they mean the 2006 film or the 1967 spoof. Never Say Never Again (1983, Sean Connery) was made outside the main series but counts.

prompt: Name as many animals that live in the Arctic or Antarctica as you can
note: Count animals that live in the Arctic or in and around Antarctica, on land, in the air or in the icy seas. Different kinds count separately (emperor and king penguins; harp and leopard seals; narwhal and beluga), and a plain 'penguin', 'seal' or 'whale' counts once too. Reindeer = caribou, orca = killer whale, ermine = stoat. Huskies and sled dogs count. Snow leopards don't (they live in the mountains of Asia). Accept any other animal that really lives there.

prompt: Name as many musical instruments as you can
note: Versions of the same instrument count once (electric and acoustic guitar; grand and upright piano). Genuinely different instruments count separately (bass guitar, double bass, bongos, timpani; handbells, sleigh bells and cowbell). The human voice doesn't count. Accept any other real instrument.

prompt: Name as many words or names that start with 'snow' as you can
note: Any real word, phrase or name beginning with 'snow' counts. Plurals, -ing forms and add-on phrases don't add an answer (snowmen = snowman, snowboarding = snowboard, snowball fight = snowball), but different things do (snow leopard, snow pea, snowy owl). 'Snow' on its own doesn't count.

prompt: Name as many car brands as you can
note: Old or discontinued brands count (Pontiac, Saab, Oldsmobile, DeLorean). Nicknames count as the brand (Chevy = Chevrolet, VW = Volkswagen, Merc or Benz = Mercedes). Accept any other real car brand, past or present. Model names don't count (Mustang, Corvette, Beetle, Civic, Golf). Brands that make only motorbikes or big trucks don't count either (Harley-Davidson, Ducati, Scania, Peterbilt), but Triumph counts because it made cars until 1984, and pickup brands like Ram and GMC count too. Car groups whose name isn't on a car badge don't count (General Motors, Stellantis).

prompt: Name as many Winter Olympic sports as you can
answers: Alpine skiing (downhill, slalom, giant slalom, super-G)
note: These are the 16 disciplines on the program of the 2026 Milano Cortina Games; ski mountaineering made its debut there. Naming an event ticks its sport (slalom = alpine skiing, moguls = freestyle skiing, ice dancing = figure skating), but each sport counts only once. 'Skiing' alone = alpine skiing, 'skating' alone = figure skating, 'hockey' alone = ice hockey, and 'Nordic skiing' = cross-country skiing. Halfpipe, slopestyle and big air are in both freestyle skiing and snowboarding: tick snowboarding if the team says snowboard, otherwise freestyle skiing. 'Sledding' and 'tobogganing' don't count: the team has to say luge, bobsleigh or skeleton. Old demonstration events don't count (ski ballet, speed skiing, skijoring).

prompt: Name as many body parts with only three letters as you can
note: Informal words count (abs, pec, lat, gob, bum, tum). Lap counts. Pit counts only as armpit. Plurals don't add an answer (arm = arms). Four-letter body parts don't count (chin, shin, knee, neck, hand, nose, foot, head). Cheeky words like bum and tum are fine; anything ruder doesn't count.
